newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Argentina explains slower budget deficit cut.
newsitem.headline: Argentina explains slower budget deficit cut.

text.p: Argentina said on Tuesday a slowing of its plan to return its budget to balance from a current deficit of two percent of GDP was because of the need for tax reform talks with Argentina's provinces.

Last week Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said that the government would now likely to target a budget deficit of 0.5 percent of gdp in 1998 rather than the previously targeted balance budget.

Fernandez told a media briefing in Melbourne that the delay in the budget-cutting plan was because of the need for negotiations with the provinces to reform the current system where the central government has to give half of its extra tax revenue to the provinces.
This meant that to reduce the budget deficit by two percentage points of gdp, the central government would have to raise taxes by four percent of gdp, he said.
This would simply result in greater spending by the provinces from their half share of the extra revenue, he said.
"We were looking at a balanced budget for 1998, but I think the discussion of the tax sharing agreement will take a little longer than that," he said.

"We will have to discuss that with the provinces so in order to find some incentive compatible tax system in such a way that just for closing the deficit we don't have a built-in mechanism for increasing expenditure," he said.
